Residents and community leaders in Bamikemo community in Ile-Oluji/Oke-Igbo Local Government Area of Ondo State have protested against the alleged imposition of a monarch on the ancient town, calling on Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa to intervene and ensure due process in the selection of their traditional ruler. The protesters accused some people in power of planning to impose a candidate they described as a stranger on the community against the wishes of the people and kingmakers. They carried placards with inscriptions such as “Governor Aiyedatiwa, save Bamikemo from imposition”; “The Akemo throne belongs to the royal blood”; “Don’t impose a stranger on us”; “We need due process for our king”; and “Don’t impose an unpopular person on Bamikemo.” Speaking after the protest on Sunday, a community leader, Oluwaseun Adewolu, alleged that some traditional rulers in Ile Oluji were attempting to impose a candidate who had no ancestral or property tied to Bamikemo. He said, “Our protest is against the imposition of somebody who doesn’t have land here; he doesn’t have a farm, doesn’t belong here, doesn’t have a house here. Somebody whose grandfather doesn’t belong here, whose father doesn’t belong here, and he himself doesn’t belong here, I don’t know why they are trying to impose such a person on us.” Adewolu described the alleged planned imposition as a violation of the community’s fundamental rights, insisting that the people should be allowed to determine who becomes their traditional ruler. He identified one Prince Adelakun Bajewolu as the preferred candidate of the town, saying his family had ancestral connections and property in the community. He added that the community had previously approached the Lisa of Ile-Iluji to express its displeasure but alleged that their concerns had not been addressed. Akingbola alleged that that the development could undermine the rights and interests of Bamikemo residents if not addressed on time. “We are pleading with the Governor of Ondo State, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, to listen to us and tell the imposers to respect the customary law, likewise the native law, and respect the lives and property of Bamikemo people,” he urged. He also identified Prince Bajewolu as the rightful candidate, alleging that excessive manipulation from Ile-Iluji had affected the community’s efforts to select its preferred monarch. Another community elder, Abdulahi Balogun, said the protesters were not seeking confrontation but wanted the government to prevent what he described as an injustice against the community. He said, “The person they want to impose on us is someone we have no connection with. I have not even seen him before in Bamikemo. He is from another town entirely, and they want him to be king over us. We wouldn’t accept that.” ‎In a reaction, the state Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Amidu Takuro, said the government had received a petition from the community on the issue, but it would not interfere in it because it was a family matter. ‎ ‎ ‎” As far as Ondo State Government is concerned, every chieftaincy matter is addressed with due process in line with the law. We don’t interfere in such matters. We received a petition from the community over the matter, but we can’t interfere because it is a family affair. That is not our responsibility. “It is the responsibility of the family to identify their son, whom they know is qualified to represent the family and the community at large. So when it comes to chieftaincy selection, we don’t interfere.” ‎ ‎ Peter Dada
